convoLines.text: "Do you believe in anything? Now, I mean. After everything."
"That's not naive. That's load-bearing. Hold onto it. I need you to hear that."
"I believe in breakfast. In people showing up. Small, provable things. The big beliefs all broke — the small ones held. Seen worse."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Hah. Still on what you believe in."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Give it time."
Tao looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"We're done for now. Not done-done. For now."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"I can't reach this properly. Could you clean it out for me? Please."
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Have you heard what they're calling Hummice? Tao is pushing 'The Loud Beast'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Groundnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Okay — I need to move. But I'm glad we talked."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About that question — What's the worst thing you've done since the sky changed?"
No judgment in their face. "We're all doing math that doesn't add up. You're still here. That counts."
Their friendliness thins — still there, just held at arm's length.
"Still on the worst thing you've done."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Otis always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
You show them Groundnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"I keep turning over the last thing Otis said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can we talk?" Catalina sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"About this wound — I hate to ask twice, but it's still open. Will you?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Otis owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Right. Action time. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About this wound — the need hasn't gone anywhere. I'm still asking."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Pantry Raid. They just... took Tao. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"My part? I oil boots on rest days and stay ready."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Serviceberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Hey — I found some Groundnut today. You were right, it was right where you said."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that plant lesson. It'll pass."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
You show them Wood Sorrel — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can we talk?" Tao sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"The pantry's nearly bare. Come forage with me tomorrow — two of us can fill packs."
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. Meet me at the meadow edge, west of the creek and we'll fill packs before dark."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Last time things were different. They always are." "David owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"My part? I remember them. Someone has to do it properly."
"Still on what's been happening."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You talk to it -- the System. Have you ever asked? About the taken -- about Karen? You're doing fine."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.

"It's my aunt, Karen. Went in the Taking. She laughed like a screen door in a windstorm. Boring. Right. Some nights I swear I hear them before I sleep -- the pods, rows deep, humming. Then morning comes and I can't say whether it was real."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? I'm listening."
"David always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Groundnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You said you believe we get through this — the alternative doesn't work. Still holding the line?"
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
"Here. I made an extra." Tao presses something into your hand — a decent tool, oiled and kept. (Useful. Keep it.)
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that personal stuff."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Yeah? What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "The Guest. They just... took Ingrid. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Alright — I should get back to it."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About what you dream about — Do you dream about before? Or is it all — this — now?"
"Then it's not gone. Not really. Keep going back."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Still on what you dream about."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took Ingrid — The Guest, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
You show them Wood Sorrel — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"We'll see what the treeline brings. We always do."
"I do the small things right. The big things notice."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

"We never finished talking about that personal stuff — we wandered off it, 7 days back. 'They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.' We still owe what's been happening a proper ending, too."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"As I said — Still on that personal stuff. You'd know about that."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Sure — what's on your mind? Just... be straight with me."
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "The Tide Clock. They just... took Aperahama. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Right. Go on, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"What do you miss most? From before."
"God. Yes. I dream about soup. Actual soup, with a spoon."
"Hot showers. Not the big things — the small, stupid, perfect things. Columbus, Ohio in the morning, coffee going, nobody trying to kill me. I miss being bored."
"Still on what you miss most."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took Aperahama — The Tide Clock, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
You show them Ghost Pipe — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."

You can feel the history in how they greet you.
"As I said — Still on what's been happening."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You're family now. Chosen family — the kind that actually counts." "That's where we are."
"Here's what it would take, if you want more than this: show up when it costs you something. That's the whole test."
"I've changed my mind about people before. Usually it takes getting hurt first. You haven't hurt me yet."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"I should go. You know where to find me."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About what happened to my taken kin — You talk to it -- the System. Have you ever asked? About the taken -- about Karen?"
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Still nothing on Karen. I told you about the pods -- I keep thinking about them. The humming. Some nights I'm sure it's a dream. Other nights I'm sure it's not."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "You want to know what I did in the raid? I stood down Big-Eyes at the treeline — it ran. Don't call it brave. Call it awake."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Yarrow — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."

d80: Snow by morning. (-7°C — Freezing) The ground goes iron — forage thin, walking dear.
d80: Tao Das reads the sky: clear tomorrow, freezing.
d80: The cold works on everyone — the village wakes aching from the deep cold.
d80: Dawn. You wake rested. (+0 health, energy restored. Your sleeping body burned less — 87 kcal conserved. By the fire. Good enough.)
